difficultyAxis: Ceiling of tier 3: four entities in two chains (Depot <- Parcel <- DeliveryAttempt and Recipient <- Parcel), eleven scenarios and the widest validation-heavy entity so far. Full CRUD plus a repeated-attempt child that carries its own sequence number.
rationale: The last blueprint before tier 4 with two entities below six attributes. It combines two foreign keys on the same child with a child-of-child chain, so resolving references is no longer a single hop, and it spends the whole tier 3 scenario budget on mixed successful and refused operations.

userStories.intent: register a depot with a country and a capacity
userStories.benefit: parcels can be dispatched from a known facility

scenarios.given: a unique depot code, a country code and a positive capacity
scenarios.then: the depot is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.given: a country code that is not two letters long
scenarios.when: the supervisor attempts to register the depot
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: register a recipient with a delivery address
userStories.benefit: the parcel has a deliverable destination

scenarios.given: a full name, an address line and a well-formed postal code
scenarios.then: the recipient is persisted with its verification flag and its address intact

userStories.intent: dispatch a parcel from a depot to an existing recipient
userStories.benefit: the shipment enters the delivery network under a tracking reference

scenarios.given: an existing recipient, an existing depot and a positive weight
scenarios.then: the parcel is persisted with both references intact and a dispatched status

scenarios.given: a recipient identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to dispatch the parcel
scenarios.then: the service reports the recipient as not found

scenarios.given: a weight below the permitted minimum
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to dispatch the parcel
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: record each delivery attempt on a parcel

scenarios.given: an existing parcel and an attempt number within the permitted range
scenarios.then: the attempt is persisted against the parcel with its outcome code

scenarios.given: an attempt number above the permitted maximum
scenarios.when: the courier attempts to record the attempt
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

scenarios.given: a parcel with no recorded attempts
scenarios.when: the courier reads the attempts for that parcel
scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error

userStories.intent: amend a parcel and withdraw a delivery attempt
userStories.benefit: the network reflects the current state of the shipment

scenarios.given: an existing parcel and a new service level
scenarios.then: the parcel is persisted with the new service level and the previous value is replaced

scenarios.given: a parcel identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the dispatcher attempts to update that parcel
scenarios.then: the service reports the resource as not found
the attempt is removed and the read that follows reports it as not found
